guide.summary: A slow fungus that eats dead material and starch, and whose new pieces start out asleep.
guide.biology: Many real fungi make tough resting cells, such as spores, that can wait through dry or hungry times and wake when conditions improve.
guide.rules: Stays attached to gel, sediment, mesh or beads and never swims. Eats detritus first, then starch, using oxygen. Stays active in drier places than other fungi, down to moisture 0.2. Each new segment starts Resting and counts as Small while resting. After 20 seconds without food, or 10 seconds with moisture too low, and with at least 15 energy, it prepares for 5 seconds and spends 10 energy, then rests: no feeding or growth, only 0.01 energy per second, and a tenth of the usual damage from poor conditions. It wakes after 10 seconds of good conditions with food and at least 5 energy, spending 5 energy over 5 seconds, and cannot rest again for 30 seconds. Comfortable at pH 4.5 to 7, warmth 0.30 to 0.65 and salinity up to 0.25. Fungal inhibitor affects it. Waterbears graze single segments, and Threadrider can attach to active segments but never resting ones.
guide.example: Let part of a gel dish dry out and compare how Sporeveil and Threadlace cope as the moisture falls.
